one_line_contribution: Admit items into an agent memory bank on their measured leave-one-out contribution inside the top-k bundle they are actually retrieved into (rather than on episode success or reflector confidence), and then audit whether the screen's own projected gain survives its estimation noise by splitting the projected-minus-realized gap into a winner's-curse term and an item-item interference term.
closest_prior_work: Two lines threaten it, and the proposal engages only the first. (i) Data-valuation-for-ICL: Nguyen & Wong (2023) influence-based example selection, plus the Data Shapley / Banzhaf-for-demonstrations line, which exists precisely because leave-one-out valuation is known to be wrong under interaction among selected examples. The proposal's 'non-additivity' finding is the standard motivation for Shapley-style estimators, so E3b's singleton-vs-LOO result would rediscover a known property of LOO valuation rather than establish a new one, and the paper never explains why LOO was chosen over the estimator the field already uses for this exact failure. (ii) Selection-on-noise in model/hyperparameter selection: Cawley & Talbot (JMLR 2010) on over-fitting in model selection and subsequent selection bias in performance evaluation is the same in-sample/unbiased/realized decomposition the paper calls its hardest-to-duplicate contribution; transplanting it to memory items with EB shrinkage is a competent application, not a new statistical result. What is genuinely unclaimed is the retrieval-neighborhood conditioning of the estimand for agentic memory; that is a real but narrow delta, and it is the piece the proposal has deliberately de-emphasized in favor of the decomposition.
strongest_objection: The headline decomposition in E3/P4 is not identified, so the paper's load-bearing claim cannot be adjudicated by the experiment as designed. Two breaks. First, retained-set mismatch: G_insample and G_unbiased are defined over 'the same retained set' from split-half probes (m approx 5.8/item), while G_actual comes from an end-to-end bank whose EB/FDR screen is fit on the full probe data (m approx 11.7). Those are different banks, so G_unbiased - G_actual mixes a genuine transfer gap with a change in the selection rule's sample size, and the 'costs zero extra episodes' oracle projection is an oracle for a bank nobody deploys. Second, and worse, bundle refill: after screening, the agent re-retrieves top-7 from the *screened* bank, so items ranked 8, 9, 10 in the original bank get promoted into bundles whose utility was never probed, and every retained item's utility was measured conditional on the presence of the very items screening removed. G_unbiased = sum of retained u_hat is therefore not an unbiased projection of realized gain even with infinite probes and perfect additivity. The residual G_unbiased - G_actual is a garbage-can term (interference + refill/promotion + neighborhood redefinition because the neighborhood is defined by the bank + train/test query shift + k shrinking below 7 in sparse neighborhoods, which reintroduces the volume lever the pilot already showed is causal). P4's refutation branch -- 'the non-additivity component dominates ... interference is implicated ... screen bundles, not items' -- is thus an unsupported attribution, and the abstract's claim that 'the mechanism is identified rather than asserted' is false as written. Two supporting problems make this worse. (a) Discreteness and coverage: 400 probe queries x 7 slots = 2,800 observations spread over 240 items under a skewed dense-retrieval distribution, so 11.7/item is a mean over a power law; a substantial tail of items will be retrieved zero or one time and have no estimable utility at all, and the proposal states no policy for what happens to never-retrieved items (retain? drop? they are also never injected at eval, which silently makes the screen partly a no-op). At split-half this is m = 0-2 for the tail, and E4's 'effective m in {2,4,7,12}' pretends m is uniform. Each observation is y_full - y_minus_m in {-1,0,+1} on EM with a 7B ReAct agent, where most probes will be concordant zeros, so most items' u_hat is exactly 0 and the ratio-of-noisy-sums quantities in P4 (>=40%, <25%, <15% of 'the naive rule's projected gain') have a denominator that can be near zero and CIs that will not exclude anything at n=240. (b) P2's 25% sign-flip threshold has no noise-matched null: two independent estimates of the *same* utility at m approx 6 would flip sign at a high rate purely from sampling, so as stated P2 cannot distinguish 'utility is neighborhood-conditional' from 'utility is unmeasurable at this budget' -- and the proposal already has the right comparator (within-neighborhood split-half A vs B) but does not use it.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Make the three G quantities share one object: fit the deployed screen on split A only, deploy exactly that bank end-to-end, and reserve split B purely as the unbiased re-estimate; report the full-data screen separately. 2) Break the residual apart instead of naming it. Add a frozen-bundle cell in which the screened items are removed from the already-probed top-7 bundles with no refill (k drops), alongside the re-retrieved screened cell; the difference isolates promotion/refill, and only what remains can be called interference. Without that cell, drop the interference language from P4 and report the residual as unattributed. 3) Give P2 a noise-matched null: compare global-vs-neighborhood sign disagreement against neighborhood-split-half sign disagreement at the identical m, and claim conditionality only on the excess. 4) Report the per-item retrieval-coverage distribution up front, pre-register the treatment of items with zero or one probe, and restate every m as a distribution rather than a mean. 5) Run the ceiling before the grid: an oracle item-level screen fit directly on the held-out set. If the oracle cannot produce +3.5 points, no realizable item-level screen can, and the 12-cell end-to-end grid should not be run -- this is a far more decisive gate than Risk 2's 'P(u>0)>0.7 for >=15% of items'. 6) Reallocate budget. The pilot's own effects were 6-7 items broken, i.e. roughly 1-2 points, yet the pre-registered claim threshold is 3.5 points; as written, 12,000 episodes are spent on twelve contrasts that are pre-declared unclaimable at the effect size the pilot actually observed. Four cells at n=3,000 would decide something; twelve at n=1,000 will not.
missing_baseline: A bundle-level selection baseline at matched probe budget -- greedy forward/backward subset selection over the bank, or a Shapley/Banzhaf-style estimator, using the same 3,200 probe episodes. This is the direct competitor implied by the proposal's own interference hypothesis, and its absence is structural: if P4's refutation branch fires and non-additivity dominates, the recommended remedy ('screen bundles, not items') has no arm in the design and the paper ends with a diagnosis and no method. All twelve end-to-end cells are item-level screens or content-blind heuristics. Secondarily missing: the oracle screen fit on the held-out set as an upper bound on what any item-level screen can deliver in this setup.
preprint_collision: The check is a non-check and must be scored as such. It reports two consecutive rounds in which every query failed with a tool error, zero titles retrieved, zero dates confirmed, and an explicitly unverified recollection list. The proposal is right to refuse to fabricate a table and right that silence is a tooling failure rather than evidence -- but under any reasonable standard novelty here is unestablished, which is a weakness and not a neutral. Named candidates the authors themselves flag and cannot date: Memory-R1-style RL memory managers (an arXiv preprint of roughly Aug 2025) and ReasoningBank-style experience distillation (roughly Sept 2025); I cannot verify those dates either and neither can the submission. The more likely collision is not in the agent-memory line at all but in demonstration/data valuation, where per-example counterfactual utility with shrinkage or influence approximations for retrieval-augmented ICL is an active 2025 area; a preprint doing per-example counterfactual valuation conditioned on the retrieved context would take the estimand contribution outright. The pre-emptive retargeting to the winner's-curse decomposition is a sensible hedge in principle, but it hedges onto the very analysis whose identification I object to above, so the fallback is weaker than the authors believe. At minimum the search must be executed before this is submittable, and the committed manual protocol (arXiv cs.CL/cs.AI/cs.LG sweeps from 2024-09, forward citations of ExpeL/MIPROv2/ReasoningBank/Memory-R1) should add data-valuation queries: 'Shapley in-context demonstration selection', 'context-conditional data valuation retrieval', 'selection bias example valuation LLM'.
